chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, and Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, all from Safwan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said:

Hamza ibn Humran married the daughter of Bukayr. So when he intended to enter with her (consummate the marriage), the women said to him, 'We will not let her come to you until you swear an oath to us.' And we are not pleased if you swear by emancipation (liberation of a slave), because you do not consider it anything. But swear to us by Zihar, and do Zihar from the mothers of your children and your female slaves. So he did Zihar from them. Then he mentioned that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said, 'There is nothing upon you. Return to them.'

key_terms.أُمَّهَاتِ أَوْلَادِكَ: Mothers of your children: Referring to the wives/mothers of the offspring, used here as the object of the Zihar oath.
key_terms.الظِّهَار: Zihar: A pre-Islamic and early Islamic form of divorce where a husband likens his wife to his mother, prohibiting sexual relations until expiation is made.
key_terms.جَوَارِيكَ: Your female slaves: Concubines or female servants, also used as the object of the Zihar oath in this narration.
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ شَيْ‏ءٌ: There is nothing upon you: A legal ruling indicating no penalty (kaffarah) is due for the specific oath made.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on swearing Zihar from the mothers of one's children or female slaves?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the flexibility of Zihar in Shia jurisprudence, where the oath is directed not at the wife herself but at her female relatives or slaves, a practice validated by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) as legally binding without penalty. It highlights the scholarly distinction between the literal wording of the oath and its legal consequences, emphasizing that the specific formulation used by Hamza ibn Humran was sufficient to establish the status of Zihar. This case serves as a key precedent for understanding how contextual intent and precise phrasing influence the application of divorce-related vows in Islamic law.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Abu Al Abbas Al Razzaz, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, altogether from Safwan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira who said,

‘Hamza Bin Humran married a daughter of Bukeyr. So when he intended to copulate with her, the women said to him, ‘We will not let her come over to you until you swear an oath to us, and we will not be pleased if you oath with the emancipation (liberation of a slave), because you do not see it as anything, but oath for us with the Zahaar, and do Zahaar from the mothers of your children, and your neighbours’. So he did Zahaar from them. Then he mentioned that to Abu Abdullahasws, so heasws said: ‘There is nothing upon you. Return to them’.
en.sarwar: 7. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar and abu al-‘Abbas al-Razzaz from Ayyub ibn Nuh all from Safwan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah who has said the following:

“Hamzah ibn Humran married daughter of Bukayr. In the night that she was to be brought to him women said to him, ‘We would not bring her to you until you swear. We will not agree to your swearing about setting free slaves because you do not consider it anything important; but you must swear about al-Zihar and form al-Zihar about the mothers of your children and slave-girls.’ He formed al-Zihar about them, then he mentioned it to abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He (the Imam) said, ‘You do not owe anything because of it and you can go back to them.’”
